items.title: UN creates task force to protect Hormuz trade as Iran tightens grip on strait

featured_image.name: Shipping slows to a crawl through Strait of Hormuz ...

items.description:
The United Nations on Friday announced the creation of a task force to safeguard humanitarian trade through the Strait of Hormuz, even as Iran moved to tighten its grip on the waterway by pursuing legislation to codify transit fees and turning back ships attempting passage.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres ordered the task force to develop mechanisms for keeping fertilizer and agricultural products flowing through the strait, which has been effectively closed since the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran began on February 28. "The prolonged closure of the Strait is choking the movement of oil, gas and fertiliser at a critical moment in the global planting season," Guterres said. The task force, led by Jorge Moreira da Silva of the UN Office for Project Services, will include representatives from the International Maritime Organization and the International Chamber of Commerce, and draws on the model of the Black Sea Grain Initiative.[1][2]

items.title: Iran strikes Israel, Gulf states as IRGC warns civilians to flee US bases

featured_image.name: Iran sends waves of missiles into Israel, dismisses Trump's talk of  negotiations as 'fake news' - The Sen Times

items.description: Iran launched fresh waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel and multiple Gulf Arab nations on Friday, the 28th day of the war that began when the United States and Israel struck Iran on February 28. As air raid sirens sounded across Israel and Gulf capitals scrambled air defenses, Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz warned that Israeli strikes on Iran would "escalate and expand," while Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued an ominous call for civilians across the region to evacuate areas near American forces.

items.title: Iran death toll tops 1,900 as IFRC warns of deepening crisis

featured_image.name: UN says nearly 22,000 civilian buildings in Iran damaged - Yahoo

items.description:
More than 1,900 people have been killed and at least 20,000 injured in Iran since the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes on February 28, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said on Friday. Maria Martinez of the IFRC, citing figures from the Iranian Red Crescent, said the organization remains the only major humanitarian body operating nationwide amid the escalating conflict.[1][2]

The death toll, which has climbed steadily over the past four weeks, marks a sharp increase from earlier estimates. By mid-March, Iranian authorities had reported roughly 1,444 deaths. The IFRC cautioned that relief efforts are continuing under severe shortages and ongoing security threats.[3][2][4][5]

items.title: Witkoff says he expects Iran talks 'this week' on 15-point peace plan

featured_image.name: U.S. envoy Witkoff says Iran is seeking an off-ramp | Reuters

items.description:
U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said Friday he expects meetings with Iran "this week" to end the month-long war in the Middle East, expressing optimism that Washington's peace framework could bring Tehran to the table. "We think there will be meetings this week, we're certainly hopeful for it," Witkoff told the Saudi-backed Future Investment Initiative summit in Miami, according to AFP. "We have a 15-point plan on the table. We expect the Iranians to respond. It could solve it all."[1]

The remarks come a day after Witkoff confirmed during a White House Cabinet meeting that the 15-point proposal had been delivered to Iran through Pakistan, which is serving as the primary intermediary. Pakistan's role as a diplomatic bridge between Washington and Tehran has become central to the nascent peace effort, even as Iran publicly rejects the American plan and fighting continues across the region.[2][3]

items.title: Iran accuses US-Israel of genocide at UN Human Rights Council

featured_image.name: Iran Foreign Minister to Address UN Human Rights Council

items.description:
Iran has made at least 20 formal communications to the International Criminal Court documenting what it calls intentional violations of international humanitarian law in the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign, the vice-president of the Iranian Red Crescent Society confirmed this week.[1][2]

Razieh Alishvandi, the deputy head of the Iranian Red Crescent Society for international and human rights affairs, said Iran has also contacted the World Health Organization and the International Committee of the Red Cross to report the scale of civilian casualties and destruction across the country. Five joint statements by the Iranian National Committee on Humanitarian Law and the Red Crescent Society have been issued documenting attacks on medical centers, ambulances, and civilians, according to Iranian state media outlet Press TV.[2][1]

items.title: US can confirm only a third of Iran's missiles destroyed

featured_image.name: US can only confirm about a third of Iran's missile arsenal ...

items.description: Nearly a month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, American intelligence assessments show the United States can only confirm the destruction of roughly one-third of Iran's vast missile arsenal, according to a Reuters exclusive citing five people familiar with the intelligence. The finding undercuts President Donald Trump's assertion at a Cabinet meeting on Thursday that Iran has "very few rockets left".[1][2][3]
